title: Gliotoxin triggers cell death through multifaceted targeting of cancer-inducing genes in breast cancer therapy.
authors: Nambiar, Sujisha S; Ghosh, Siddhartha Sankar; Saini, Gurvinder Kaur
one_liner_zh: 该文研究真菌代谢物胶霉毒素通过多靶点抗癌基因诱导乳腺癌细胞死亡，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白相互作用而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Fungal secondary metabolites have a long history of contributing to pharmaceuticals, notably in the development of antibiotics and immunosuppressants. Harnessing their potent bioactivities, these compounds are now being explored for cancer therapy, by targeting and disrupting the genes that induce cancer progression. The current study explores the anticancer potential of gliotoxin, a fungal secondary metabolite, which encompasses a multi-faceted approach integrating computational predictions, molecular dynamics simulations, and comprehensive experimental validations. In-silico studies have identified potential gliotoxin targets, including MAPK1, NFKB1, HIF1A, TDP1, TRIM24, and CTSD which are involved in critical pathways in cancer such as the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, MAPK/ERK signaling pathway, hypoxia signaling pathway, Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, and other essential cellular processes. The gene expression analysis results indicated all the identified targets are overexpressed in various breast cancer subtypes. Subsequent molecular docking and dynamics simulations have revealed stable binding of gliotoxin with TDP1 and HIF1A. Cell viability assays exhibited a dose-dependent decreasing pattern with its remarkable IC(50) values of 0.32, 0.14, and 0.53 muM for MDA-MB-231, MDA-MB-468, and MCF-7 cells, respectively. Likewise, in 3D tumor spheroids, gliotoxin exhibited a notable decrease in viability indicating its effectiveness against solid tumors. Furthermore, gene expression studies using Real-time PCR revealed a reduction of expression of cancer-inducing genes, MAPK1, HIF1A, TDP1, and TRIM24 upon gliotoxin treatment. These findings collectively underscore the promising anticancer potential of gliotoxin through multi-targeting cancer-promoting genes, positioning it as a promising therapeutic option for breast cancer.
abstract_zh: 真菌次生代谢产物在药物开发中有着悠久的历史，尤其在抗生素和免疫抑制剂的研发中贡献显著。利用其强效生物活性，这些化合物目前正被探索用于癌症治疗，通过靶向并破坏诱导癌症进展的基因。本研究探讨了胶霉毒素（一种真菌次生代谢产物）的抗癌潜力，采用了一种整合计算预测、分子动力学模拟和全面实验验证的多方面方法。计算机模拟研究已识别出潜在的胶霉毒素靶点，包括MAPK1、NFKB1、HIF1A、TDP1、TRIM24和CTSD，这些靶点参与癌症中的关键通路，如NF-kappaB信号通路、MAPK/ERK信号通路、缺氧信号通路、Wnt/beta-catenin通路及其他重要细胞过程。基因表达分析结果显示，所有识别出的靶点在多种乳腺癌亚型中均过表达。随后的分子对接和动力学模拟揭示了胶霉毒素与TDP1和HIF1A的稳定结合。细胞活力测定显示出剂量依赖性下降模式，其对MDA-MB-231、MDA-MB-468和MCF-7细胞的IC(50)值分别为0.32、0.14和0.53 μM。同样，在3D肿瘤球体中，胶霉毒素表现出显著的活力下降，表明其对实体瘤的有效性。此外，使用实时PCR的基因表达研究显示，胶霉毒素处理后，癌症诱导基因MAPK1、HIF1A、TDP1和TRIM24的表达减少。这些发现共同强调了胶霉毒素通过多靶向癌症促进基因的潜在抗癌能力，使其成为乳腺癌治疗的一个有前景的选项。
